subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native memory trust/provenance contract should OpenClaw support for durable memory ingestion, persistence, retrieval, review/expiration gates, and plugin/MCP interop?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the durable data model, trust assignment authority, retrieval enforcement semantics, config shape, and external plugin/MCP boundary are security- and compatibility-sensitive product choices.

options.title: Define native memory trust contract
options.body: Keep this issue open and design source, review, expiration, influence, and provenance fields that OpenClaw memory backends and plugins must preserve before coding.

options.title: Adopt external prior art as optional plugin path
options.body: Document AKF/world-model-mcp-style integrations as optional ClawHub/MCP solutions while leaving native memory behavior unchanged for now.

options.title: Fold into broader responsibility-gates umbrella
options.body: Make the broader owner-signed responsibility issue the canonical design owner and close or narrow this issue only after the memory-specific contract is represented there.

recommendation.title: Define native memory trust contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and design source, review, expiration, influence, and provenance fields that OpenClaw memory backends and plugins must preserve before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current routing signal for the memory host SDK and memory-core contract boundary, plus prior review context on this issue.
